subject: Early delivery SLA, streaming chunk cadence & pilot plan
messages:
From: Alice Gellman <alice.gellman@quantivox.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Quantivox Engineering <engineering@quantivox.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: latency targets and streaming cadence (recap)

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and the signal we promised: Quantivox is shipping a collaborative doc editor where users expect near-real-time typing and cursor updates that include model-generated suggestions. We need to align on TTFT and chunk cadence so we can map to UX thresholds. Key items from our side: 

- TTFT targets: median TTFT <= 180ms; p95 <= 450ms for typical prompts (10-50 tokens of priming + user input).
- Chunk cadence: we want sub-200ms chunk cadence for streaming partial suggestions (smooth character-by-character feel). If that isn't feasible, we accept 250-300ms but prefer lower.
- Concurrency/throughput: expected steady-state is ~350 concurrent users on the pilot, peak bursts up to ~1.2k concurrent for demos. Typical payloads are small (<150 tokens).
- Mode: prefer SSE for simplicity and CDN compatibility but open to WebSocket if cancellations and low-latency user control are better supported.
- Fallbacks: on large cold-model startup we need a graceful fallback (e.g., smaller cached model or stub suggestions) rather than blocking the UI.

Attaching a short requirements doc and a sample prompt set. Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet the TTFT/p95 targets on your hosted tier or whether we should plan Dedicated capacity for the pilot? Also, what instrumentation do you need from us (sample traffic, synthetic tests, tokenization examples)?

Thanks — happy to sync further this week.

Best,
Alice Gellman
VP Product, Quantivox
attachments: Quantivox_streaming_requirements.pdf, QVOX_sample_prompts.json

--
On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 14:45 Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the quick call earlier — sending intro materials.
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gellman <alice.gellman@quantivox.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency targets and streaming cadence (recap)

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear targets — this helps a lot. High-level answers up front: 

- Feasibility: The TTFT median <= 180ms and p95 <= 450ms are achievable for the majority of prompts on our hosted platform with proper priming and prefix caching. For sustained high burst concurrency (1.2k) we typically recommend Dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbors, though we can run an initial pilot on hosted with caps.

- SSE vs WebSocket: For your use case where CDN compatibility and per-request simplicity matter, SSE is the lower-opportunity-cost choice. If you need client-driven cancellations or bidirectional UX, WebSocket gives more control. We'll propose both in the pilot.

- Chunk cadence: We can target ~100–200ms chunk emission for small responses once the KV cache is warm. Cold-starts can be an order of magnitude slower (we'll mitigate with priming and a warm pool).

- Fallbacks: We support automatic fallback routing to smaller quantized variants to preserve interactivity during cold starts — we'll document the tradeoffs in UX quality vs latency.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Redwood runs a 5k-request synthetic probe using your sample prompts (you'll share sample traffic shapes).
2) We'll run a 72-hour pilot on hosted (traffic-limited) to verify p95/median and chunk cadence; if we observe degradation under burst we switch to a Dedicated pilot.
3) Technical handoff call with Aditya and Markus to align on test harness and instrumentation (trace IDs, token counts).

Can you confirm: sample traffic (CSV or gzipped JSON), preferred pilot start window (next 2 weeks), and a drive link for shared telemetry? Once you confirm we'll produce a pilot runbook with explicit SLO check points.

Thanks — I'll loop engineering for the handoff.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency targets and streaming cadence (recap)

Steph / Markus —

Technical notes for the handoff and what we'll ask QVOX to provide before we run the probes: 

- Priming & tokenization: include the exact prompt templates and any system messages. If prompts include long context, we should precompute token counts; short user-only prompts are cheaper.
- Prefix/KV warming: to hit sub-200ms chunk cadence you need a warm KV cache for the common priming pattern. Suggest a warm pool (up to N warm workers) during the pilot window.
- Batching/continuous batching: we can keep per-request latency low while gaining cost efficiency by configuring small, time-bounded batches (e.g., 4–8ms micro-batching window). We'll instrument batch size and queue delay.
- Model variants: recommend two variants for the pilot — an 'interactive' (low-latency, fp16/8-bit quantized) and a 'quality' variant. Fallback rule: prefer interactive until quality delta > threshold.
- Concurrency sizing: for 1.2k peak concurrent small payloads, estimate 3–4 p3-equivalent GPU units for 90% of traffic if using interactive variant (ballpark; will profile).
- Measurement plan: measure TTFT (server accept -> first chunk emit), chunk inter-arrival distribution, p50/p95/p99, and end-to-end user-perceived latency (browser render loop). We'll need trace IDs and a small sample of production traffic (~10k requests) or synthetic equivalent.

I'll prepare a short runbook with commands to run our synthetic harness (wrk-style) and the tracing decorators we want in the payload. Can we get the sample payloads and an expected concurrency curve?

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — sounds good. We can: 

- Share sample traffic (we'll drop a gzipped JSON with 12k synthetic requests into the Drive link you provided).
- Target pilot start: Sept 28 — gives our SRE time to provision a sandbox and configure client-side tracing.
- Confirm we prefer SSE initially. We'll add a WebSocket path if we see client cancellation spikes during the pilot.

Link to shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qVox-Pilot-Shared (access granted to redwood.oncall@redwood.com).

We'll also sign the pilot terms (DocuSign link when you send the runbook). For instrumentation, we'll add a header x-qvox-trace-id and include token counts in the body.

Looking forward to the handoff.

Best,
Alice
VP Product, Quantivox
